text.title: Semantic Constraint Gap Failure Modes
text.summary: Six ways the gap between a compiled grammar and a written schema shows up in production, each with the observable symptom and the rule that prevents it.

failure.symptom: Every response parses, the schema check is green in CI, and downstream code still receives values it was written to assume impossible — a score of 1.7, an empty required-looking string, a justification three screens long.
failure.cause: The team read the repo schema and believed it. The wire copy the provider compiled contained neither the range nor the length, because the SDK helper stripped them into the field `description`.
failure.prevention: Rename the signal. "Schema valid" means parseable; say so on the dashboard, then add the checks that mean correct.

failure.symptom: Nobody can answer "is this constraint enforced?" without reading provider docs, and the answer differs per field.
failure.cause: A single schema file serves as both wire contract and validation contract, so the enforced subset is implicit and drifts every time a field is added.
failure.prevention: Two files, two names, one record naming both. The diff between them IS the post-validation checklist.

failure.symptom: A defect class is known to exist and has zero incidence in every report, because the code that catches it writes a log line and continues.
failure.cause: The check was implemented as defensive hygiene rather than as a measurement, so no counter, no assertion and no user-visible output was attached.
failure.prevention: Every dropped keyword gets a counter. Observed live in faion-cli `internal/search/agent.go:270` (2026-08-03): hallucinated identifiers are dropped correctly and counted nowhere.

failure.symptom: An identical prompt and schema produce a malformed value on one provider and never on another; the bug will not reproduce until someone notices which transport was routed.
failure.cause: Gemini's OpenAPI subset compiles `pattern` and numeric ranges; Anthropic's grammar does not. One transport was silently doing the validation the code never did.
failure.prevention: Declare the transport list, take the union of drop sets, and post-validate at the strictest level everywhere.

failure.symptom: A feature that wants parseable output AND provider-emitted citations dies with a 400 the first time both are switched on, usually late, usually in the one code path that assembles the full request.
failure.cause: The incompatibility is documented on the Citations page and not on the Structured Outputs page (both fetched 2026-08-03), so a team building from the latter cannot learn it before the error.
failure.prevention: Design as two calls from day one — schema-constrained ID selection, then citations-enabled prose over exactly those bodies. It is also the better design: the selection stays machine-checkable and the prose stays citable.

failure.symptom: Weeks spent pushing schema compliance from 99.2% to 99.8% while user-visible wrongness is unchanged.
failure.cause: Compliance is the metric the tooling reports for free, so it becomes the metric that is optimised. Value accuracy has no default dashboard.
failure.prevention: Compliance is already near-saturated across 21 models while exact leaf-value accuracy sits at 83.0% on plain text (arXiv:2604.25359, 2026-04-28). Move the budget to the values.
